# KS-1135 MANIFESTQUARANTINESTDERR-1 MAKE A RED IN `manifest_quarantine.test.sh` DIAGNOSABLE — WHEN ANY CELL FAILS, PRINT THE tsx DRIVER'S STDERR TAIL BEFORE THE EXIT TRAP REMOVES IT WITH `$TMP` — one line of the suite changed (`cleanup()`), no product file, no cell added — Wednesday's task for Ornith, TEST_ONLY, **ONE existing bash suite, one hunk (one line replaced), no product file** (written 2026-09-21 15:5x after the #1119-#1128 batch gate; its NOT-PINNED row MANIFESTQUARANTINESTDERR, "the leg-14 intermittent (item 3 / 14) … a row for the RECORD (Polish / ticket candidate for Wednesday)"; **briefed under KS-1135 — see the provenance note in the raise section: no ticket names this row; KS-1135 is the nearest live ticket and names the same class**)

File: `systemTest/__tests__/manifest_quarantine.test.sh`
Tip: `9f0265eb06ecf24d4de18149ce862ad2330a61ee`

Written from develop `9f0265eb06ecf24d4de18149ce862ad2330a61ee` (`git -C "/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/2_Project_Files" ls-remote origin refs/heads/develop` at 15:30 on 2026-09-21, read verbs only; the tree `23d60cace7c3` that carries the ten #1119-#1128 squashes). The suite at that tip is **200 lines** (blob `2ae67f244ddd`), read whole; its full content is in `files[...]` of your input. It lives at the REPOSITORY ROOT under `systemTest/` (not under `Blockchain/Dev/`) and drives the real `quarantineManifest()` of `systemTest/fixtures/manifest.ts` (172 lines; `export function quarantineManifest(provisionedAt: string, target: string = manifestPath())` at `:137`, `if (!fs.existsSync(target)) return null;` at `:138`, `const dir = path.dirname(target);` at **`:139`**) through a throwaway `npx tsx "$TMP/drive.ts"` driver written at `:41-:46`. Runner: **bash** (a `*.test.sh` suite, run by the checker as `/bin/bash <file>` from the clone root, bash 3.2.57; `tsx` comes from the npx cache — no install, no network on this machine).

## THE MODE — read this twice

**TEST_ONLY.** Your diff touches EXACTLY ONE file: the suite above, MODIFIED IN PLACE (`--- a/<path>` / `+++ b/<path>`, the path exactly as written above — it starts with `systemTest/`, NOT with `Blockchain/`). You never touch `systemTest/fixtures/manifest.ts` or any other file: no product behaviour changes and no cell is added — the ONE line that changes is the suite's own `cleanup()`.

## What the change does (one paragraph)

Every cell of this suite reads the driver's STDOUT (`moved="$(… npx tsx "$TMP/drive.ts" … 2>>"$TMP/driver.err")"`) and appends its STDERR to `$TMP/driver.err` — at SEVEN sites (`:82`, `:119`, `:131`, `:145`, `:147`, `:172`, `:191`; the eighth `driver.err` mention, `:60`, is the KS-1078 comment that says the streams are separated). Nothing ever PRINTS `driver.err`: the only stderr shown is the harness probe's `probe.err` (`:66-:70`), and the EXIT trap (`:32-:34`: `TMP="$(mktemp -d)"`, `cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP"; }`, `trap cleanup EXIT`) removes `$TMP` — `driver.err` with it — before anyone can look. So when a driver run dies (tsx could not start, the module threw, a socket/IPC failure under load), its stdout is empty, the cell prints `returned ''` or `got ''`, and the one thing that would say WHY is gone. That is what the #1119-#1128 gate hit on #1125's first push: leg 14 of the pre-push preflight went red on this suite once, never again serially (0/3, 0/2), and the red was un-diagnosable — MANIFESTQUARANTINESTDERR, "a row for the RECORD". This change replaces the ONE `cleanup()` line: when at least one cell has failed (`$FAIL -gt 0`, the counter `bad()` increments at `:30`) AND `driver.err` is non-empty, print a one-line header and the LAST 40 lines of `driver.err`, each prefixed `     | ` (five spaces, a bar, a space — deeper than any cell line, so no reader or parser mistakes them for cells), then remove `$TMP` exactly as before. A green run prints nothing new (`FAIL` is 0); a red run with a silent driver prints nothing new either (`-s` is false); a red run whose driver wrote to stderr now shows it, after the tally, in the same log.

**Why `cleanup()` and not `bad()`, said plainly (a deviation from the gate row's letter):** the row proposed printing `tail -5 "$TMP/driver.err"` "beside `returned '…'`", i.e. inside `bad()` at `:30`. That line is followed by the blank `:31`, and a hunk that ends on `:30` has no non-blank trailing context (strict `git apply` refuses a mid-file hunk with none — measured: `patch does not apply`; the harness never uses `--unidiff-zero`), and a blank context line is never in a fence. `cleanup()` at `:33` sits between two non-blank, unique lines and is the ONE place that already knows the file is about to disappear — one line, all seven sites covered, the tail printed once at exit instead of once per failed cell (with nine driver runs appending to one file a per-cell `tail -5` would show the same last lines anyway). `tail -40` rather than `-5` because a tsx failure is a ~18-line stack trace and the file is shared by all nine runs — 40 keeps the last two traces whole.

## The exact change — ONE hunk in the suite

ONE `-` line, ONE `+` line, with ONE leading context line (`:32`, `TMP="$(mktemp -d)"`) and ONE trailing (`:34`, `trap cleanup EXIT`) — each unique in the file. The `+` line KEEPS the original removal (`rm -rf "$TMP"; }`) as its last statement, byte for byte; everything added sits in front of it inside one `if … fi;`. Copy every line byte for byte. The `+` line is ASCII only, carries NO backslash, no backtick, no template, and no `printf` — `echo` for the header (the string starts with two spaces and the word `driver`, so `echo` is safe), `tail -40` for the lines, `sed 's/^/     | /'` for the prefix (single quotes; five spaces, `|`, one space). `$FAIL` is the counter `:27` declares (`PASS=0; FAIL=0`), so under `set -u` it is always set when the trap fires. There is no blank line anywhere in the fence. Keep the header exactly as shown. **Your diff MUST begin with the two file-header lines, above the `@@` line: `--- a/systemTest/__tests__/manifest_quarantine.test.sh` then `+++ b/systemTest/__tests__/manifest_quarantine.test.sh`.**

```
@@ -32,3 +32,3 @@
 TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
-cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP"; }
+cleanup() { if [ "$FAIL" -gt 0 ] && [ -s "$TMP/driver.err" ]; then echo "  driver stderr (tail -40 of driver.err, shown because $FAIL cell(s) failed; the EXIT trap removes it next):"; tail -40 "$TMP/driver.err" | sed 's/^/     | /'; fi; rm -rf "$TMP"; }
 trap cleanup EXIT
```

Do NOT touch `bad()` (`:30`), the probe block (`:66-:72`), any `2>>"$TMP/driver.err"` site, or the tally lines (`:198-:200`). Do NOT add a `printf` (its format would need a backslash). Do NOT change `tail -40` to another number or `sed`'s prefix to another string: the checker holds you to the `+` line above byte for byte.

## Cells

- `stale_gone` = `the stale manifest is gone from the path consumers read`
- `copy_exists` = `a superseded copy exists`
- `copy_content` = `the superseded copy still carries the stale content (moved, not deleted)`
- `copy_named` = `the copy is named for the rejecting run AND its slot`

- `first_content` = `the first quarantine still holds its own content`

## Red cells

No cell is ADDED by this diff — the seven cells below already exist at the tip and are GREEN there; they are declared as the red set of the tamper below, which models the exact failure this change exists to diagnose (a driver that dies mid-suite), and they are named by the literal prefixes the suite prints on its `ok`/`FAIL` lines.

## Tampers

One single-line tamper on the product the driver imports, `systemTest/fixtures/manifest.ts:139` — the line AFTER the existence check: it appends a `throw` that fires only for a September stamp (`provisionedAt.startsWith('2026-09')`). The `From` occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the file as a whole line (python whole-line scan: 1 hit at 139). The `To` is valid TypeScript (one statement added after the existing one; tsx transpiles and runs it — measured: seven driver runs die with the thrown error, nine run). **Why the condition:** the suite's four `slot $slot: …` cells (`:170-:177`) print a `$slot`-EXPANDED description that is not literally in the file, so the harness cannot name them; the slot loop and the default-path cell (`:189-:195`) use the `2026-01-01` stamp while the seven cells above use `2026-09-07` stamps, so a September-only throw reds exactly the seven nameable cells and leaves the two CONTROLs (their path does not exist — `:138` returns `null` before the throw), the four slot cells and the default-path cell green. **The tamper is the leg-14 symptom made deterministic:** the driver's stdout is empty (`returned ''` / `got ''`), its stderr carries the stack trace, and at the tip that trace is deleted with `$TMP`; with this hunk it is printed under the tally. The checker plants it and restores the file by bytes.

At the untouched tip the suite is `14 passed, 0 failed`, rc 0, and prints nothing from `driver.err` (measured — `FAIL` is 0, the `if` is false, the trap only removes `$TMP`); with this hunk it is STILL `14 passed, 0 failed`, rc 0, and prints nothing new (measured). #!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for quarantineManifest() in systemTest/fixtures/manifest.ts
#   KS-969 F1, round 3
# =============================================================================
# The defect this exists for: a rejected provisioning run DECLINED TO WRITE a
# manifest and called that a fallback. It is not. `generated/` is gitignored and
# survives across runs, so a manifest published by an earlier pass stays exactly
# where every consumer looks for it. A NON-WRITE IS NOT A REMOVAL.
#
# It was live when this was written: actors.json (seed presuite-test-72460,
# 07:57:14Z) beside actors.rejected.json (seed presuite-strict-47722, 08:50:37Z)
# -- the newer run refused, the older manifest still the one being read.
#
# These cells run against a TEMP DIRECTORY on purpose. The sibling suite creates
# five real accounts on any stack answering on :6882 and overwrites the real
# manifest (KS-973 item 3); this one must not add to that, so it touches no
# stack and no shared file.
#
# Usage: bash systemTest/__tests__/manifest_quarantine.test.sh
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
FIXTURES="$HERE/../fixtures"
PASS=0; FAIL=0

ok()  { PASS=$((PASS+1)); printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; }
bad() { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); printf '  FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "${2:-}"; }

TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP"; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# The driver imports the real function and points it at a temp path, so the
# cells exercise shipped code rather than a re-implementation of it.
# The import is ABSOLUTE: the driver lives in $TMP, so a relative specifier
# would resolve against the temp directory and tsx would fail with an empty
# stdout -- which reads exactly like "the function returned nothing".
cat > "$TMP/drive.ts" <<TSEOF
import { quarantineManifest } from '$FIXTURES/manifest.ts';
const [, , stamp, manifestPath] = process.argv;
const moved = quarantineManifest(stamp, manifestPath);
process.stdout.write(moved === null ? 'NULL' : moved);
TSEOF

# Fail loudly if the driver itself cannot run. Without this the suite cannot
# tell "quarantine returned nothing" from "tsx never started", and every cell
# below would report the same empty string.
#
# KS-1078: the redirect here MUST be `2>"$TMP/probe.err"`, never `2>&1`.
# It was `2>&1`, which folded stderr INTO the value compared against "NULL" —
# so anything at all written to stderr failed the comparison and was reported as
# "the tsx driver did not run". On a clean runner with no local tsx, `npx` prints
#     npm warn exec The following package was not found and will be installed: tsx@…
# and the probe became "npm warn …\nNULL": the driver had run and returned the
# right answer, and the guard called it a launch failure. That is what reddened
# `Code Security Gates` on every PR. The rest of this file already separates the
# streams (`2>>"$TMP/driver.err"`); the probe was the one place that did not.
#
# The compared value is the driver's stdout and nothing else. stderr is still
# SHOWN in the diagnostic below — a guard whose whole purpose is telling
# "returned nothing" from "never started" needs stderr visible, not swallowed
# and not silently merged into its own verdict.
if ! probe="$(cd "$FIXTURES" && env -u SECUURA_STACK_SLOT -u STACK_SLOT -u SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX npx tsx "$TMP/drive.ts" '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z' "$TMP/does-not-exist.json" 2>"$TMP/probe.err")" \
   || [ "$probe" != "NULL" ]; then
  printf '  FAIL harness: the tsx driver did not run\n'
  printf '     stdout: %s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$probe" | head -3)"
  printf '     stderr: %s\n' "$(head -3 "$TMP/probe.err" 2>/dev/null)"
  exit 1
fi

echo "== manifest.ts quarantineManifest =="

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A pre-existing manifest is MOVED ASIDE, and its content goes with it.
# This is the cell that fails against a fix that merely skips the write.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
M="$TMP/actors.json"
printf '{"seed":"stale-run","actors":{}}\n' > "$M"
moved="$(cd "$FIXTURES" && env -u SECUURA_STACK_SLOT -u STACK_SLOT -u SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX npx tsx "$TMP/drive.ts" '2026-09-07T08:50:37.940Z' "$M" 2>>"$TMP/driver.err")"

if [ ! -e "$M" ]; then ok "the stale manifest is gone from the path consumers read"
else bad "the stale manifest is gone from the path consumers read" "still at $M"; fi

if [ -n "$moved" ] && [ "$moved" != "NULL" ] && [ -f "$moved" ]; then
  ok "a superseded copy exists"
else
  bad "a superseded copy exists" "returned '$moved'"
fi

# MOVED, not deleted -- the copy must still carry the stale content, otherwise
# this is a delete wearing a rename's name.
if [ -f "${moved:-/nonexistent}" ] && grep -q 'stale-run' "$moved"; then
  ok "the superseded copy still carries the stale content (moved, not deleted)"
else
  bad "the superseded copy still carries the stale content (moved, not deleted)" "$moved"
fi

# The name must carry the rejected run's stamp, so two quarantines are tellable
# apart by a human reading the directory.
#
# KS-971: it carries the SLOT too, between the prefix and the stamp — a stamp alone is not
# unique across concurrent slots. This driver runs with no SECUURA_STACK_SLOT, which is slot 1,
# so the expected name is `actors.superseded-slot1-<stamp>.json`. The pre-KS-971 form
# (`actors.superseded-<stamp>.json`) is asserted ABSENT below, so a regression to it is a
# failure and not merely a different green.
case "${moved:-}" in
  *actors.superseded-slot1-2026-09-07T08-50-37-940Z.json) ok "the copy is named for the rejecting run AND its slot" ;;
  *actors.superseded-2026-09-07T08-50-37-940Z.json) bad "the copy is named for the rejecting run AND its slot" "pre-KS-971 name, no slot: '${moved:-}'" ;;
  *) bad "the copy is named for the rejecting run AND its slot" "got '${moved:-}'" ;;
esac

# Under an explicit slot the tag follows it — the whole point of carrying it. Same stamp, slot 3:
# the file must NOT collide with the slot-1 copy above.
M3="$TMP/actors-slot3.json"
printf '{"seed":"stale-run-3","actors":{}}\n' > "$M3"
moved3="$(cd "$FIXTURES" && env -u STACK_SLOT -u SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=3 npx tsx "$TMP/drive.ts" '2026-09-07T08:50:37.940Z' "$M3" 2>>"$TMP/driver.err")"
case "${moved3:-}" in
  *actors.superseded-slot3-2026-09-07T08-50-37-940Z.json) ok "slot 3's copy carries slot3, so the same stamp on two slots cannot collide" ;;
  *) bad "slot 3's copy carries slot3, so the same stamp on two slots cannot collide" "got '${moved3:-}'" ;;
esac

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CONTROL -- no pre-existing manifest. Without this cell, a fix that
# unconditionally deleted or created something would pass everything above.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
EMPTY="$TMP/empty"; mkdir -p "$EMPTY"
before="$(ls -1 "$EMPTY" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
res="$(cd "$FIXTURES" && env -u SECUURA_STACK_SLOT -u STACK_SLOT -u SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX npx tsx "$TMP/drive.ts" '2026-09-07T08:50:37.940Z' "$EMPTY/actors.json" 2>>"$TMP/driver.err")"
after="$(ls -1 "$EMPTY" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"

if [ "$res" = "NULL" ]; then ok "CONTROL: with no manifest present it reports nothing moved"
else bad "CONTROL: with no manifest present it reports nothing moved" "returned '$res'"; fi

if [ "$before" = "$after" ]; then ok "CONTROL: with no manifest present it creates nothing"
else bad "CONTROL: with no manifest present it creates nothing" "$before -> $after"; fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# An existing quarantine is NEVER clobbered -- overwriting one would be
# deleting it under another name, and the rule is move, never delete.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
printf '{"seed":"first-stale","actors":{}}\n' > "$M"
first="$(cd "$FIXTURES" && env -u SECUURA_STACK_SLOT -u STACK_SLOT -u SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX npx tsx "$TMP/drive.ts" '2026-09-07T09-00-00-000Z' "$M" 2>>"$TMP/driver.err")"
printf '{"seed":"second-stale","actors":{}}\n' > "$M"
second="$(cd "$FIXTURES" && env -u SECUURA_STACK_SLOT -u STACK_SLOT -u SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX npx tsx "$TMP/drive.ts" '2026-09-07T09-00-00-000Z' "$M" 2>>"$TMP/driver.err")"

if [ "$first" != "$second" ] && [ -f "$first" ] && [ -f "$second" ]; then
  ok "a second quarantine at the same stamp does not clobber the first"
else
  bad "a second quarantine at the same stamp does not clobber the first" "first='$first' second='$second'"
fi

if [ -f "${first:-/nonexistent}" ] && grep -q 'first-stale' "$first"; then
  ok "the first quarantine still holds its own content"
else
  bad "the first quarantine still holds its own content" "$first"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# KS-682 x KS-971: the superseded copy carries its SLOT. KS-682 saw the defect on
# the slot-4 rotation 2026-09-10 (a DEGRADED run on slot 4 moved its manifest aside
# under a slot-less name -- attribution lost, and two slots quarantining in one
# millisecond would collide). KS-971's name is the one that survived the develop
# merge of PR #900 (2026-09-11): `actors.superseded-slot<N>-<stamp>.json`, the slot
# taken from SECUURA_STACK_SLOT, for every slot including slot 1.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "== superseded copy carries its slot (KS-682 x KS-971) =="
for slot in 1 2 3 4; do
  M="$TMP/actors-slot$slot.json"; printf '{"seed":"s%s","actors":{}}\n' "$slot" > "$M"
  moved="$(cd "$FIXTURES" && env -u STACK_SLOT -u SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=$slot npx tsx "$TMP/drive.ts" '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z' "$M" 2>>"$TMP/driver.err")"
  case "$(basename "${moved:-}")" in
    actors.superseded-slot$slot-2026-01-01T00-00-00-000Z.json) ok "slot $slot: superseded copy is actors.superseded-slot$slot-<stamp>.json" ;;
    *) bad "slot $slot: superseded copy carries its slot" "got '$(basename "${moved:-}")'" ;;
  esac
done

# The default path must resolve at CALL time, not import time (the frozen
# MANIFEST_PATH flagged on #896): set the slot after import, quarantine with no
# path argument, and the file moved must be that slot's.
cat > "$TMP/drive-default.ts" <<TSEOF
import { quarantineManifest } from '$FIXTURES/manifest.ts';
process.env.SECUURA_STACK_SLOT = process.argv[2];
process.stdout.write(String(quarantineManifest('2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z')));
TSEOF
# manifestPath() names fixtures/generated/actors-slot<N>.json relative to the fixtures dir;
# use slot 4 and put a throwaway file there, then restore whatever was present.
G="$FIXTURES/generated"; mkdir -p "$G"; had=""; [ -f "$G/actors-slot4.json" ] && { had=1; cp "$G/actors-slot4.json" "$TMP/keep-slot4.json"; }
printf '{"seed":"default-path-probe","actors":{}}\n' > "$G/actors-slot4.json"
moved="$(cd "$FIXTURES" && env -u SECUURA_STACK_SLOT npx tsx "$TMP/drive-default.ts" 4 2>>"$TMP/driver.err")"
case "$(basename "${moved:-}")" in
  actors.superseded-slot4-*.json) ok "default path resolves at call time: slot set after import quarantines THAT slot's manifest" ;;
  *) bad "default path resolves at call time" "got '$(basename "${moved:-}")'" ;;
esac
rm -f "$G"/actors.superseded-slot4-2026-01-01T00-00-00-000Z*.json "$G/actors-slot4.json"; [ -n "$had" ] && cp "$TMP/keep-slot4.json" "$G/actors-slot4.json"

echo
printf '  %s passed, %s failed\n' "$PASS" "$FAIL"
[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
